notes:
• Android, a trial: in a Front Desk call a podcast, music or a video in another app pauses while the Front Desk or you speak and goes on once both have been quiet for 5 s, instead of playing on under the call. Your voice is told from noise by a speech detector on the phone (Silero VAD); nothing leaves the phone for it. The call card's new Media button switches between pausing, lowering (music turns down, podcasts pause) and leaving other audio alone. A Bluetooth headset now takes the call when it starts or connects (Android 12+). The iPhone keeps pausing other audio for the whole call for now.
• Claude accounts in one place. Mac: Settings → Account lists the Claude accounts (moved from Agents) with "Add Claude account…", which signs in via claude.ai like on a team host (or takes a token), and below them what happens when limits run out (moved from the Usage tab, which now says which rules are on and has a Settings… button). Team host: each person can add several Claude accounts (iOS, Android, Mac) and sets their own rules for the limits, including "Use when switching" per account (off for a private one); their messages run on the active one and, with switching on, carry on with their next account that has room. Older apps keep a single Claude row; their "Sign out" removes all of a person's accounts.
• Stacked PRs on GitHub's own stacks: "Start from" → "Stack on pull request…" (Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android, and `stellwerk://new?stack=`) starts a new branch from the PR's branch, targets it, and puts the new PR on top of it in GitHub's stack. A stacked PR shows its stack under the git bar ("main ← #42 ← #43", tap one to open its workspace or the PR), says "Ready after #42" instead of offering Merge while the one below is open, merges through GitHub's stack merge, and once the one below merged offers what's left: Sync with GitHub's rebase, Retarget, or Rebase without the merged PR's commits (asked first, force-push with lease). Any workspace whose PR targets another branch now compares to that branch, so Changes match GitHub's "Files changed".
• Git bar: Automerge shows again while checks run, on repositories with GitHub's "Allow auto-merge" on (it never showed since the own host replaced Conductor).
• Closing a chat no longer asks first (tab ✕, ⌘W, chats menu; Mac, iOS, Android): it stays in the closed chats history and reopens from there.
• Mac: ⌘W closes the open tab (chat, file or subagent) and no longer closes the window when there's no tab to close, which hid Stellwerk like quitting. ⇧⌘W closes the window.
• Mac: a background command's tooltip shows the whole command, not just its first 120 characters (the host cut it short).
• iOS and Android: the workspace list's title is the Mac's name with its menu, always in the bar, so switching Macs works without scrolling (no big "Workspaces" title any more). A Mac without a name shows its address there, on both.
• Mac: back in a workspace, it looks as you left it: the right panel's tab (Changes, All files, Checks), the open file tab, All files' open folders, also after a restart; while the app runs also the subagent tab, All files' filter and where the file, its diff and the panel's lists were scrolled to.
• The Mac host's web server and crypto libraries get their latest security fixes, and the Android app's libraries and build tools are updated.
• Mac connected to a team host: "Pair a phone as you" is on the Devices page now (Account points there), with your name and avatar and which of your sign-ins on the host the phone uses.
• Team host chats (Mac, iOS, Android): the people row with the avatars shows only once someone besides you wrote in the chat or has it open.
• Mac: an image attachment's preview over its pill in the message box stays while the pointer is on the pill instead of popping up and vanishing, and goes below the pill where there's no room above.
• Mac Settings: rows that belong together sit in groups with a small title, indented beside a line. Account: Claude accounts with "When limits run out" inside (on a team host also "You on …"); Devices: Phones and Team; Agents: Programs; Front Desk: Voice and audio, Brain and memory, Calls; General: Messages.
• Mac setup: the first step picks Private host, Team host or Connect to another Mac and goes on. On a team host the Claude, GitHub and Entire logins are marked optional (everyone signs in from their own phone or Mac). Settings while the window shows another Mac leave out this Mac's host pages (models, git, agents, environment, Front Desk, repositories, host rows of Account, Devices, Advanced), list that Mac's repositories and say on each page which Mac it's about.
